reviews.title: Apple Health integration is abysmally bad
reviews.text:
I love the treadmill, the app is pretty good too. Except that their integration with Apple Health is absolutely abyssmally bad. 

They don’t write active energy, and instead you end up with whatever calories Apple calculates off the watch which basically makes it impossible to accurately track calories burned. 

Trying to use Strava is an intermediary results in duplicate workouts being created. 

The Apple Watch requires that you enable workout writing in order to be able to use it as heart rate monitor, so you can’t even stop the duplicate and partial data work by cobbling together a solution with multiple apps.  

I’ve used both Hydrow and peloton and neither one has these problems, so I know it can work properly, but apparently iFit has no interest in actually making it work. 

Incredibly frustrating that they would miss such a basic fundamental capability.

reviews.title: Service, yikes.
reviews.text: This used to be a 5-star review.  My treadmill broke down nearly a year ago (on extended warranty) and they’ve been jerking me around ever since. A tech has been to my house 5 TIMES to replace different parts, with no effect. I spent another 90 minutes on the phone today, with repeated holds and transfers, only to have the last person tell me sorry, the service rep hasn’t written a note yet, and everyone has left for the weekend. All I can say is, if you buy an IFIT product, you better just hope it doesn’t break down, because trying to get it fixed is a protracted, mind-bending nightmare. The tech who now know the way to my house without directions is experienced and helpful, but IFit and their warranty contractor UTS have been terrible.

reviews.title: Buyer beware

When I went to try and cancel this account, I was unable to do so as I don’t have the information to that account. I called them and was told that they would cancel it for me. I explained that I’ve never used this account and they could check to see this account had not been used. I only had the free version. They stated they were unable to do anything for me since it was a year ago. I explained again that I was not aware that this account was open. They still stuck to company policy of they could not do anything for me. If I did not call, I would’ve been charged 149.99 for an account I can’t use. Talk about a scheme. I asked how much I had paid for this account and was told $99 so basically they took $100 from me for an account that I could not use and was going to charge me 149.99 to renew it.  Doesn’t sound like a company I want to do business with.

reviews.title: Really disappointing
reviews.text: I bought a new Nordic track treadmill last year. The treadmill has been great. However, this app is really disappointing in a couple of ways. Despite the fact that I paid full price for the treadmill, it continually tries to get me to opt in to a paid monthly subscription every time I use it. I cannot disable this or tell it I’m not interested. I am a competitive runner and I have my own workouts planned. A second major issue I have is with data exportability. It is a legal requirement in the state I’m in (and many other states as well as Europe) for customers to be able to export their data from software platforms like this. iFit has always made this difficult, burying this in settings menus, but in their recent website redesign they appear to have removed this ability entirely. I was told by their AI support bot that there is no longer any way to get the data exported from my workouts. I am frustrated and disappointed with this application and their apparent disregard from people who just want to use the treadmill to run and have access to their workout data.

reviews.title: Almost amazing
reviews.text: Love the workouts from the convenience of home without even having a machine to pair with...yet. Unfortunately I’ve had glitches with the calendar and syncing despite multiple calls/contact with tech support and fixing it. Things appear and disappear on my calendar and continue to not sync over devices- this makes tracking my workouts and finding favorites difficult and frustrating. I hope it gets better. Update: some of the syncing is better, but still not great. Also, you used to be able to stream your music through a work out but now you’re stuck with their music or just listening to the talking. I really only seemed like the spotlight workouts and if I wasn’t grandfathered in on the lower price I don’t recommend that at all. I thought it might be good for new people, but the trainers seem to assume a lot of things that I know as a previous trainer and if you’re brand new to working out, it might be awkward. i’m glad they have the pause feature but even that used to be you could pause it and still have access until the end of your billing cycle but now they just turn it off right away and you don’t get any money back.Customer service across the board is kind of a joke. I had to get a different story depending on who you talk to if you can even get a person on the phone sooner than an hour.

reviews.title: Apple Watch HR Streaming Sucks!
reviews.text:
Leaving this review until SW updates improve. Overall fitness selection & workouts are great, but the phone / watch integration with my X24 tread is horrible. Every time I start workout trying to stream heart rate (HR) data from watch to the treadmill the iFit app either 1. never connects to watch app or 2. disconnects within a few seconds to minutes of being connected and streaming HR data. Even worse, the only way to get it to reconnect is to completely abandon your workout and start a new one, it doesn’t have the ability to reconnect mid-session, you have to ‘start’ a workout for it to think to look for the apple watch to connect to. Really hope this improves because the UX is horrible and totally kills the workout experience. I have other comments about integrations with Apple Health & Strava:
- AH: iFit uploads everything on the tread as an outdoor run, even if it’s walking pace, there’s no way to change this setting (even in custom workouts) (in what world is a workout on a tread ever an outdoor run???)
- Strava/iFit: if you link both it will upload to strava, then strava will upload to apple health, then iFit will pull from Apple health and basically double track your workout everywhere. Have to setup a single flow of data because iFits unable to screen for the same exact workout and prevent double counting.

reviews.title: QR code error
reviews.text: I have tried for months to connect my ifit elliptical to my account. Note you can now only sign in through a QR code. For the life of me my entire family, friends, neighbors tried to connect our device just to receive a VPN error. We did a hard reset of device, disconnected all VpN, connected through PC, cellular, iPad, iPhone you name it without any luck. I lost all my experiences and can no longer sign in. I tried to get live help just to be told the same AI version over and over. After paying for a pro membership for years I received useless customer service. Almost 3 months later and no phone call back from support I give up. Save your frustrations and buy a fitness program that still gives you the option of live support and cares to help you connect your account. Waste of time and money!

reviews.title: Terrible software and horrible customer service

They took down their website about six months ago, that was where you could manage your calendar, find other challenges, conveniently create your own maps etc. On the app, only about four months of the calendar appears. Good luck contacting them with issues. It seems like it’s bots that respond. They don’t even answer what your question is, just give a blanket response that means nothing. You can’t even get a personal membership on the app. Even if single you are required to buy a family plan. Every time I turn my treadmill on I find it has a different random date, today it was November 15; and there’s no easy way to change it. Run away from this company.

reviews.title: Latest update made it useless for cycling!
reviews.text:
Update: Got a response from iFit developers stating that current RPM is available from the drop down, like i’m some sort of idiot who didn’t check for that before leaving a review... iFit developers, go back and check your work, because as I stated there is no longer a current rpm readout, only target and average. We need to be able to see our current RPM (like we could in all versions until the big update / new look) if we are to follow the trainer’s instructions! How do we know how hard / fast to pedal if we can’t see our “current rpm?!” SMH 

Clearly the team who redesigned this app have never used any of the cycling workouts. The current RPM readout has been removed. Only average and target RPM remain. So when the trainer says I need you at 100 RPM, you no longer have any idea what your pedal speed is because you can only get an average over the whole ride. I will not be renewing unless this is fixed. This update made ifit pointless for me.

reviews.title: Not VPN friendly at all
reviews.text:
Even though I’m based in the UK and my VPN server I connect to is based in the UK, I very rarely get the chance to have my iPhone app connect to the Apple watch app. It’s always the phone app that fails due to my VPN. Because i have poor phone reception indoors i use WiFi calling, but to secure wifi calling and my DNS, i use a VPN. I have to manually disconnect my phone from my WiFi, then turn off the VPN, then walk outside to get a signal to connect to mobile, then start the iFit app on my phone, and I always have to relogin, then go back indoors, then turn my VPN back on, then connect to my WiFi again, then retstart the Nordic Track treadmill to kickstart the connection again. It’s a nightmare when all i want to do is run and watch Netflix while having my BPM monitored. Wish I’d never bought the Nordic track tbh. The connection will stay ok for a few days or a week and then i have to do it all over again. When i just want to get on the treadmill and run … waste of my time.
CN someone at iFit explain to me why I need my phone at the treadmill to have my treadmill read my BPM from my watch?! 
Update: now even my work around doesn’t work. Rendering the iFit app on the watch, useless. Rendering the iFit app on my phone, useless.
Response to dev: I have 1 phone, 1 watch, and 1 treadmill - all with hardware IDs you could use to monitor our usage and to prevent unauthorised use of your subscriptions, or unauthorised sharing, or whatever your reasons are for banning VPNs. To outrig

reviews.text: I keep clicking to resume the next session, ant otvtakes me to something completely different. Frustrating and time wasting.

reviews.title: Screen lockout after updates
reviews.text:
After recent updates the Ifit app opens to a blank screen. This happens on iPad and iPhone. Delete, reboot and restore does not fix the issue. Now left with a subscription that can’t be used!
Everything had been working well for the last 5 years

reviews.title: Terrible app!
reviews.text: Cannot connect the app to my X24 bike. After multiple requests from customer service to help I’ve been met with silence - my advice is buy a peloton!

reviews.title: Great workouts, absolutely rubbish app!
reviews.text:
The workouts themselves are very good, but the app has serious syncing and navigation problems.

I am currently doing the Australian Walking/Running series with John Peel, which I really enjoy, and I am on the last workout. However, when I open the app on my iPhone, the Home screen keeps pushing a dumbbell workout series that I don’t want to do. This workout seems stuck on my account and keeps being promoted instead of showing my actual next workout.

Because of this, my real next session in the running series does not appear on the Home screen, and I have to dig through menus to find it. The app also auto-adds workouts to my calendar that I did not choose, and there is no option to remove them.

Another issue is that I cannot find or create a manual workout anymore.

I have tried reinstalling the app, logging out and back in, and joining other programmes, but nothing fixes it.

The training content is excellent, but the app experience needs improvement, especially around Home screen recommendations, programme management, and navigation

reviews.title: Poor search. Poor user interface
reviews.text: My heart rate has now just stopped syncing from my Apple Watch. This app isn’t supported by a decent tech team and changes are badly rolled out. The search function is rubbish and barely shows all the results. Plus the filtering options are poor.

reviews.title: Does not work since update
reviews.text: I just get a black screen when I open this app on my iPad. Tried rebooting but same result - nothing

reviews.title: Connection issues
reviews.text:
The app used to work seamlessly with Apple health logging all my bike workouts. Since end of November 2025 this has stopped. The app on my phone and watch connect to the bike and log all workouts  but will not transfer the data to my health app so I’m now having to log it manually. 
Please can you fix this issue. It’s been 3 months now!!

reviews.title: Can’t use this with new IOS
reviews.text: I downloaded the new iOS and now the app is not working, can’t get any support, very poor

reviews.title: Rock bottom
reviews.text: This app has been getting progressively worse and worse for months.  For the past 3 weeks it won’t even open.  Tried on 3 different iPad Pros.  I’m literally paying for a service you’re not even providing.  Beyond a joke.

reviews.title: Workouts spoiled
reviews.text: App was amazing but recent update has taken away actual cadence in bike mode and replaced with average. As most lessons require specific cadence this has ruined the workouts.

reviews.title: Smart adjust doesn’t work
reviews.text: The smart adjust feature doesn’t work on the elliptical. It does the opposite of what it is meant to do. When in a rest period, the resistance goes up to 16. When in a work period, it goes way down to 8. When you see the trainer go up an incline, the resistance goes down and it should go up. It means you constantly have to override the smart adjust and alter the resistance manually. So frustrating and disruptive. Can we turn this feature off or choose the old “follow trainer” system which worked perfectly well. A classic case of AI making things worse, not better.

reviews.title: Ram
reviews.text: Stopped syncing with apple health for over a month. Latest update did not fix it.

reviews.title: App doesn't open!
reviews.text: App fails to open every single time. Just a blank screen. Used to be ok.

reviews.title: Was a Great App but upgrade made it not function with my equipment
reviews.text: I have used iFIT for over 5 years since I bought my ProForm hybrid elliptical/recumbent bike. The vast majority of my workouts were elliptical ones. Great trainers in amazing locations. Since the App was upgraded in 2nd half of 2025 it no longer allows me to sync for elliptical workouts. I have reported this but iFIT team have not been able to resolve the issue. They also have not offered a refund for over 6 months of use where I have to manually control my machine.

reviews.title: Please fix
reviews.text: No longer syncs with Apple Health data so my workouts don’t show up on my iPhone. Please fix!

reviews.title: App gone downhill
reviews.text: Have used iFit for over a year, enjoy the workouts etc. keeping myself fit. But recently the app has gone majorly downhill. No longer syncs to Apple health after a workout, have tried numerous things, all permissions accepted, but still nothing. Have to manually input data on phone, which defeats the object really. Disappointing considering monthly subscription is quite a lot. Hopefully they will fix this soon, as reading online in forums this appears to be a major issue with other Apple users. Not good.

reviews.title: AI trainer
reviews.text: The AI trainer is completely useless.  It can’t understand the meaning of, workouts every other day nor can it understand the type of work out I want, instead it just puts random schedules into the calendar that are nothing like I want. It can’t remove the incorrect schedule from the calendar after it’s put it in there incorrectly.  I have broken down what I want and when I want it and when it schedules something incorrectly and I tell it that it’s wrong, it apologises and says it wants to learn and get things right for me. It’s a complete joke. I tried to report the problem from the ‘report an issue’ tab in the app but the app tells me it’s unable to submit.

reviews.title: Can’t even open app
reviews.text: Downloaded app, black screen, tried contact support team but no help

reviews.title: Ifit bricked my bike
reviews.text: I’ve been using my proform Tour de France manually for the last year or so.  There’s no update section, no internet access via WiFi (It doesn’t have Bluetooth) and I can’t play music on the 2 biggish speakers.  Even the stage videos have been deleted by the last update.  Thanks guys…. £1500 down the plug hole!

reviews.title: Hard to use and too easy
reviews.text: The app is terrible, hard to find your routines, a nightmare syncing to the device and everything is too easy.. I’m not fit and it’s all a walk in park AI coach says he makes it harder but he never does.. disappointing as I’ve spend £2k on equipment tied into it

reviews.title: New app not great
reviews.text: Ever since the app updated a couple months ago, it’s not worth the money. Spending £300+ on something that no longer syncs up to your equipment, makes you log out of accounts to switch profiles in family accounts, and doesn’t load full workout libraries is not worth the money anymore, which is such a shame as after 4 years, Im considering switching to Peloton. Even deleting and reinstalling doesn’t work. One star for the app, but 5 stars for the trainers (the only reason I haven’t cancelled yet).

reviews.title: Frequently Fails
reviews.text: Despite having an excellent WiFi connection this app frequently fails in that when downloading it just shows a rotating circle which continues for ages! During this time one cannot escape back to the apps menu. Really disappointing!
